newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Traded down amid weak buying support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Traded down amid weak buying support.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was traded down on Wednesday on worries over reduced buying from a local trading company, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $96 per tonne for August 8-12 lifting and a 380-cst cargo for August 11-15 exchanged hands at $94 per tonne.
The 180-cst was last traded on Monday at $99 per tonne and the 380-cst grade was traded at $95.50 on Tuesday.
Traders said concerns over decreasing buying interest from the local trader weighed the market and may continue putting prices under pressure.
The local trader had bought more than 12 cargoes over the past month.
Although the trader was in the market on Wednesday, there were still worries that he might not continue to support prices.
On Wednesday, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said it sold 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur, 180-cst fuel oil for August 4-8 lifting at around $100 per tonne.
Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp also sold by tender 20,000 tonnes of fuel oil to British Petroleum at a discount of $14.75 per tonne to Singapore spot quotes for July 22-23 lifting.
"Both results are not very good because supplies are quite sufficient now," said one trader, seeing prices edging lower Singapore.
But some traders were not as pessimistic.
"Crude is holding well and the other markets are not falling. I don't see chances for prices to fall further," said another trader.
